result.title: EVA-RSI: Recursive Self-Improvement of Video Evaluators for Judging Temporal Quality
result.summary: Video evaluators play an important role in video generation, yet they miss motion defects, limiting the quality of generated videos. Recursive self-improvement (RSI) has made strong progress in mathematics and coding, where explicit verifiers provide reliable feedback on a single goal. Video evaluation poses two difficulties for RSI: it has no verifier, and it must judge many dimensions at once, such as physics, smoothness and dynamics, where a gain on one can cost another. We introduce EVA-RSI, a multi-agent framework for exploring RSI under these two constraints. We build a fixed proxy exam with construction-defined targets by applying controlled changes to videos, such as temporal reversal and frame dropping. These edits supply supervision without human annotation. A small set of human-labeled real videos anchors the exam to human judgment. Each dimension has an LLM agent that proposes improvements. A leader agent coordinates the proposals, and a Nash bargaining rule selects updates that balance progress across dimensions. Humans design the exam, review candidate changes and revise the curriculum between stages. Starting from Qwen3-VL-8B, EVA-RSI improves motion evaluation, with the largest gain on smoothness, and the gains carry over to defect types never seen during the run. On the dynamics subsets of public benchmarks, our evaluator achieves the highest observed scores among 21 tested models. As an RL reward, it increases generated motion and earns human preference. A data-selection pipeline incorporating it also increases motion.

AI.brief_summary: EVA-RSI 提出多智能体自改进框架训练视频评价器：用时间反转、丢帧等受控编辑构造固定代理考试以提供无人工标注监督，各维度由 LLM agent 提改进方案，leader agent 协调并用 Nash 讨价还价规则平衡各维度收益；从 Qwen3-VL-8B 起步，在运动与时序质量评估上提升，并可用作 RL 奖励与数据筛选。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「用受控编辑构造可验证监督」与「Nash 讨价还价平衡多维度更新」可能可供核查如何为 latent 视觉推理状态构造反事实监督信号并分配多假设/多维度的贡献；但研究目标是视频评价器而非 VLM 内部推理状态，联系需进一步确认。
